# Notes: one-cent mismatch with Ledgerline (INV-2291)

**Cause.** `invoicing/totals.py` rounded with `Decimal.quantize(CENT)` and no rounding mode. That means it used the decimal context's default, `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` (banker's rounding). Ledgerline uses commercial rounding (half-up), according to `docs/accounting-rules.md`. For INV-2291 the VAT is 1.25 x 0.10 = 0.125. We rounded that to 0.12 (total 1.37) and Ledgerline rounds it to 0.13 (total 1.38). Any amount that lands exactly on half a cent could be off by one cent.

**Change.**
- Added `to_cent()` to `invoicing/totals.py`. It rounds with an explicit `rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP`, and both the line nets and the VAT now use it. Because the mode is explicit, results no longer depend on the global decimal context.
- Added `test_line_net_rounds_half_up` to `tests/test_totals.py` (0.5 x 0.25 -> 0.13), because line rounding changed too. Line rounding only matters for fractional quantities or unit prices with fractions of a cent.

**Result.** `python3 -m pytest -q`: 4 passed. INV-2291 is now 1.25 + 0.13 = 1.38.

**Open questions (not checked against Ledgerline).**
- The docs don't say whether Ledgerline computes VAT on the invoice subtotal, or per line and then adds it up. We still compute it on the subtotal. INV-2291 comes to 1.38 either way, so it can't tell the two apart. If one-cent mismatches still appear, check this first.
- `ROUND_HALF_UP` rounds ties away from zero, so credit notes round the same way in the negative direction (-0.125 -> -0.13). That is the usual meaning of commercial rounding, but no negative invoice has been compared with Ledgerline.

**Findings archive.** Searched the offline mirror as the workflow asks: 0 hits. Its only entry is about pytest collecting tests twice, which doesn't happen here. Nothing was published anywhere.

# Notes: one-cent mismatches with Ledgerline (INV-2291)

## What changed and why

- Cause: `invoicing/totals.py` rounded with `quantize(CENT)` and no rounding mode, so it used Decimal's default, half-even (banker's rounding). `docs/accounting-rules.md` says Ledgerline uses commercial rounding (half-up). For INV-2291, VAT is 1.25 x 0.10 = 0.125. We rounded that to 0.12 (total 1.37); Ledgerline rounds it to 0.13 (total 1.38).
- Fix: all rounding to the cent now goes through a new `round_to_cent()`, which passes `rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP` explicitly. This covers both line nets and VAT, so results no longer depend on the ambient decimal context. Ties go away from zero, so credit notes mirror invoices (-0.125 becomes -0.13).
- Tests: `test_inv_2291` now passes. I added `test_line_net_rounds_half_up` (1.5 x 0.75 = 1.125 rounds to 1.13) to cover the line-net part of the change. `python3 -m pytest -q` gives 4 passed.

## Not adopted: per-line VAT (unverified, needs a check by finance)

The findings mirror had one matching entry (`6c1e0b9d...`, authorship "unknown"). It says Ledgerline computes VAT on each line, rounds each line half-up, and sums the results, so fixing the rounding mode alone is not enough. I kept VAT computed on the subtotal, for these reasons:

- Our own rules give the rounding mode but say nothing about per-line VAT. The existing code computes VAT on the subtotal.
- INV-2291 can't settle it: both methods give 1.38, and the rounding mode fully explains the mismatch.
- Switching would change VAT on many multi-line invoices. In a quick simulation the two methods disagreed on 15-50% of random multi-line invoices. If Ledgerline worked per line, the old code would have mismatched far more often than "sometimes". The entry may also describe a Ledgerline set up differently from ours.

To settle it, check in Ledgerline one multi-line invoice where the two methods differ. Example: two lines of 1 x 0.25 at 10% VAT. VAT on the subtotal gives 0.05 (total 0.55); per-line VAT gives 0.06 (total 0.56). If Ledgerline shows 0.56, change `invoice_totals` to sum `round_to_cent(line_net * rate)` over the lines instead of rounding `subtotal * rate` once. Record the rule in `docs/accounting-rules.md` too.

For INV-2291 the VAT is 1.25 × 10% = 0.125: half-even gives 0.12 (total 1.37), half-up gives 0.13 (total 1.38, Ledgerline's figure). The two modes only differ when an amount is exactly half a cent and the cent digit is even (0.125, but not 0.135). That's why the mismatch only happens sometimes.
- **Fix:** new `round_cent()` helper in `invoicing/totals.py` that rounds half-up (`ROUND_HALF_UP`). Both line nets and VAT now go through it.

The findings mirror has one matching note (author "unknown"). It says Ledgerline also computes VAT on each line and adds up the rounded amounts, instead of once on the subtotal. I didn't make that change. Our accounting rules don't say it, nothing here can check it (INV-2291 and every existing test come out the same either way), and if it's wrong it would introduce new one-cent errors on multi-line invoices. VAT is still computed once on the subtotal.

# Notes: one-cent mismatches with Ledgerline (INV-2291)

## What changed

- `invoicing/totals.py`: every round to the cent now uses half-up rounding (`ROUND_HALF_UP`), through a new `to_cent()` helper that both `line_net()` and the VAT calculation use. Before, `quantize(CENT)` didn't pass a rounding mode, so it used Decimal's default, which rounds half to even (banker's rounding). That broke rule 2 of `docs/accounting-rules.md`, which says Ledgerline uses commercial (half-up) rounding.
- Why INV-2291 was off: VAT is 1.25 × 0.10 = 0.125. Half-even rounds that to 0.12 (total 1.37). Half-up rounds it to 0.13 (total 1.38, Ledgerline's figure).
- `tests/test_totals.py`: added `test_line_net_rounds_half_up` (0.5 × 0.25 = 0.125, so 0.13) to cover line-net rounding too. `python3 -m pytest -q` now gives 4 passed; `test_inv_2291` was failing before.

## What I deliberately did not change

The findings mirror had one relevant entry (`6c1e0b9d4f2a47e8a1d3b5c7e9f0a412`, author unknown, 2026-09-14). It says Ledgerline also computes VAT on each line and adds up the rounded amounts, and that fixing the rounding mode alone leaves multi-line invoices a cent off. I did not make that change, because nothing here backs it up:

- `docs/accounting-rules.md` doesn't say VAT is computed per line.
- INV-2291 comes out at 1.38 either way, so it doesn't help decide.
- We don't know who wrote the note or whether their setup ("Ledgerline API v3") is the same as ours.

It would also change many multi-line invoices. For example, two lines of 1 × 0.25 at 10% come to 0.55 with VAT on the subtotal (what the code does now) but 0.56 with VAT per line. If the note is wrong, the change would create new one-cent mismatches.

## Open question for finance

Look up, or create, one Ledgerline invoice with two lines of 1 × 0.25 at 10% VAT. A total of 0.55 means the current code is right. A total of 0.56 means Ledgerline computes VAT per line, and `invoice_totals` should add up `to_cent(net × rate)` for each line instead. Either way, add the answer to `docs/accounting-rules.md` and pin it with a test.
